title: Introduction to Deep Learning: From Historical Context to Modern Applications

cues.en: -: Allison should know.
cues.zh: 艾莉森應該知道。

cues.en: -: What is Internet anyway?
cues.zh: 網際網路到底是什麼？

cues.en: -: Internet is a massive computer network.
cues.zh: 網際網路是龐大電腦網路。

cues.en: -: The one's that becoming really big now.
cues.zh: 現在變得很大的那個。

cues.en: -: What do you mean? How does one-- What do you write to it like mail?
cues.zh: 什麼意思？怎麼……像寫信寄給它？

cues.en: -: No, a lot of people use it and communicate.
cues.zh: 不是，很多人用來溝通。

cues.en: I guess they communicate, with NBC writers and producers.
cues.zh: 我想他們和 NBC 作者、製作人溝通。

cues.en: Allison, can you explain what Internet is?
cues.zh: 艾莉森，可以解釋網際網路嗎？

cues.en: ("Symphony no. 5")
cues.zh: （第五號交響曲）

cues.en: -: How amazing is that?
cues.zh: 講師：多驚人？

cues.en: Just over twenty years ago people didn't even know what the Internet was, and today we can't even imagine how lives have fared.
cues.zh: 二十多年前，人們連網際網路是什麼都不知道，今天無法想像沒有它的生活。

cues.en: Welcome to the Deep Learning A-Z course.
cues.zh: 歡迎來到 Deep Learning A-Z。

cues.en: My name is Kirill Eremenko, and along with the co instructor, Hadelin de Ponteves, we're super excited to have you on board.
cues.zh: 我是 Kirill Eremenko，和共同講師 Hadelin de Ponteves，都很高興你加入。

cues.en: And today we're going to give you a quick overview of what deep learning is, and why it's picking up right now.
cues.zh: 今天快速介紹深度學習是什麼，為何現在興起。

cues.en: So let's get started. Why did we have a look at that clip, and what is this photo over here?
cues.zh: 開始吧。為何看那片段，這照片是什麼？

cues.en: Well, that's clip was from 1994, this is a photo of a computer from 1980, and the reason why we're kind of delving into history a little bit is because
cues.zh: 片段是 1994 年，照片是 1980 年電腦；稍談歷史，因為

cues.en: neural networks, along with deep learning, have been around for quite some time.
cues.zh: 神經網路與深度學習存在已久。

cues.en: And they only started picking up now and impacting the world right now.
cues.zh: 但到現在才開始興起、影響世界。

cues.en: But if you look back at the 80s, you'll see, even though they were invented in the 60s and 70s, they really caught on to a trend or caught wind
cues.zh: 回看八〇年代，雖然六〇、七〇年代就發明，但真正流行

cues.en: in the 80s.
cues.zh: 是在八〇年代。

cues.en: So people started talking about them a lot, there was a lot of research in that area and everybody thought that deep learning or neural networks were this new thing that
cues.zh: 大家開始熱烈討論、很多研究，都認為神經網路或深度學習是會

cues.en: is going to impact the world, that is going to change everything, that is going to solve all the world's problems.
cues.zh: 影響世界、改變一切、解決世界問題的新事物。

cues.en: But then, it kind of slowly died off over the next decade.
cues.zh: 但之後十年逐漸退燒。

cues.en: So what happened? Why did, why did the neural networks not survive and not change the world?
cues.zh: 發生什麼？為何沒生存下來、改變世界？

cues.en: Was it the reason was that they were just not good enough?
cues.zh: 只是因為不夠好？

cues.en: That they're not that good at predicting things?
cues.zh: 不善於預測？

cues.en: And not that good at modeling, and basically just not a good invention?
cues.zh: 不善建模，基本上不是好發明？

cues.en: Or is there another reason?
cues.zh: 還是其他原因？

cues.en: Well, actually there is another reason.
cues.zh: 其實有其他原因。

cues.en: And the reason is in front of us, it's the fact that technology back then was not up to the right standards to facilitate neural networks.
cues.zh: 就在眼前，當時技術不足以支援神經網路。

cues.en: In order for neural networks and deep learning to work properly, you need two things: You need data, and you need a lot of data.
cues.zh: 要讓神經網路與深度學習正常，需要兩樣：資料，而且大量資料。

cues.en: And you need processing power. You need strong computers to process that data and facilitate the neural networks.
cues.zh: 還有運算力，強大電腦處理資料、支援網路。

cues.en: So let's have a look at how data or storage of data have evolved over the years.
cues.zh: 看看資料或儲存如何演進。

cues.en: And then we'll take a look at how technology has evolved.
cues.zh: 再看技術。

cues.en: So here we got three years: 1956, 1980, 2017.
How did storage look back in 1956?
cues.zh: 1956 儲存如何？

cues.en: Well, there's a hard drive, and that hard drive is only a 5, wait for it, megabyte hard drive.
cues.zh: 這是硬碟，只有五，聽好了，MB。

cues.en: That's 5 megabytes right there.
cues.zh: 這裡只有 5 MB。

cues.en: On the forklift, the size of a small room, that's a hard drive being transported to another location on a plane,
cues.zh: 在堆高機上，小房間大小，正用飛機運到別處，

cues.en: and that is what storage looked like in the 50s, in 1956.
cues.zh: 這是五〇年代、1956 年的儲存。

cues.en: You had to pay, a company had to pay two and a half thousand dollars of those days' dollars to rent that hard drive.
cues.zh: 公司得付當時每月 2,500 美元租它。

cues.en: To rent it, not buy it, to rent it for one month.
cues.zh: 是租，不是買，一個月。

cues.en: In 1980, the situation had improved a little bit.
cues.zh: 1980 改善一點。

cues.en: So here you got a 10 megabyte hard drive for three and a half thousand dollars.
cues.zh: 10 MB 硬碟，3,500 美元。

cues.en: And still very expensive, and only 10 megabytes, so that's like one photo these days.
cues.zh: 仍很貴，只有 10 MB，現在一張照片大小。

cues.en: And today in 2017, we've got a 256 gigabyte SSD card for $150, which can fit on your finger.
cues.zh: 錄製的 2017 年，256 GB SSD 卡，150 美元，放得上手指。

cues.en: And if you're watching this video, a year later, or like in 2019, or 2025, you're probably laughing to yourself because, by then, you'll even have an even stronger storage capacity.
cues.zh: 若一年後，或 2019、2025 年看，可能自己笑，因為儲存更強。

cues.en: But, nevertheless, the points stands. If you compare these across the board, and without even taking price and size into consideration, just the capacity of whatever was trending at the time.
cues.zh: 但重點仍成立，不考慮價格與尺寸，只比較當時熱門的容量。

cues.en: So from 1956 to 1980, capacity increased about double, and then it increased about twenty, five thousand
cues.zh: 1956 到 1980 大約兩倍，再增加二萬五千

cues.en: six hundred times.
cues.zh: 六百倍。

cues.en: And the length of the period is not that different.
cues.zh: 期間長度差不多。

cues.en: So from 1956 to 1980, twenty-four years, from 1980 to 2017, thirty-seven years, so not that much of an increase in time.
cues.zh: 1956 到 1980 二十四年，1980 到 2017 三十七年，時間沒多那麼多。

cues.en: But a huge jump in technological progress, and that stands to show that this is not a linear trend.
cues.zh: 但技術大跳躍，表示不是線性。

cues.en: This is an exponential growth in technology.
cues.zh: 而是指數成長。

cues.en: And if we add into taking account of price and size, it will be in the millions of increase.
cues.zh: 若再計價格尺寸，提升會是數百萬倍。

cues.en: And here we actually have a chart on an algorithmic scale.
cues.zh: 這裡有對數刻度圖。

cues.en: So if we plot the hard drive costs per gigabyte, you'll see that looks something like this.
cues.zh: 畫每 GB 硬碟成本，像這樣。

cues.en: We're very quickly approaching zero.
cues.zh: 很快接近零。

cues.en: Right now, you can get storage on Dropbox and Google Drive, which doesn't cost you anything.
cues.zh: 現在 Dropbox、Google Drive 可以取得免費儲存。

cues.en: Cloud storage and that's going to continue.
cues.zh: 雲端儲存，會持續。

cues.en: And in fact, over the years, this is going to go even further.
cues.zh: 未來更進一步。

cues.en: Right now, scientists are already looking into using DNA for storage, and right now, it's quite expensive. It costs $7,000 to
cues.zh: 科學家已研究 DNA 儲存，目前很貴，合成

cues.en: synthesize 2MB of data, and then another $2,000 to read it.
But that kind of reminds you of the whole situation with the hard drive and the plane.
cues.zh: 讓人想到硬碟與飛機。

cues.en: That this is going to be mediated very, very quickly with this exponential curve.
cues.zh: 這種指數曲線會很快改善。

cues.en: Ten years from now, twenty years from now, everybody's going to be using DNA storage if we go down this direction.
cues.zh: 若照這方向，十、二十年後人人會用 DNA 儲存。

cues.en: Here are some stats around that, so you can explore as further.
cues.zh: 一些統計，可深入。

cues.en: Maybe pause this video if you want to read more about this.
cues.zh: 想讀可暫停。

cues.en: This is from nature.com, and basically, you can store all of the world's data in just 1 kilo, 1 kilogram of DNA storage.
cues.zh: 來自 nature.com，基本上只一公斤 DNA，就能存全世界資料。

cues.en: Or you can store about 1 billion terabytes of data in 1 gram of DNA storage.
cues.zh: 一公克大約十億 TB。

cues.en: So that's just something to show how quickly we're progressing, and that this is why deep learning is picking up now. That we are finally at the stage where we have enough
cues.zh: 這只是展示進展有多快，也是深度學習現在興起原因；終於有足夠

cues.en: data to train, super, super cool, sophisticated models.
cues.zh: 資料訓練非常酷、精密的模型。

cues.en: Back then, in the 80s, when it was first initiated, that just wasn't the case.
cues.zh: 八〇年代最初不是如此。

cues.en: And the same thing we talked about is processing capacity.
cues.zh: 運算能力也是。

cues.en: So here we've got an exponential curve again on a log scale.
cues.zh: 對數刻度上一樣有指數曲線。

cues.en: It's not ideally portrayed here, but in the right, you can see a log scale.
cues.zh: 這裡呈現不完美，但右側可見對數刻度。

cues.en: And this is how computers have been evolving.
cues.zh: 電腦就是這樣演進。

cues.en: So, again, feel free to pause this slide.
cues.zh: 可暫停。

cues.en: This is called Moore's Law, you've probably heard of it.
cues.zh: 叫摩爾定律，可能聽過。

cues.en: How quickly the processing capacity of computers has been evolving.
cues.zh: 電腦運算能力如何快速演進。

cues.en: Right now, we're somewhere over here where an average computer can buy for a thousand bucks.
cues.zh: 現在約在這裡，一千美元普通電腦，

cues.en: Thinks at the speed of the brain of a rat, and between '25, it'll be the speed of a human,
cues.zh: 思考速度像老鼠大腦，到 2025 像人，

cues.en: or 2023, or by 2050, or 2045, it will surpass all of the humans combined.
cues.zh: 或 2023；到 2050 或 2045，會超越所有人類總和。

cues.en: So, basically we're entering the era of computers that are extremely powerful.
cues.zh: 基本進入極強電腦時代。

cues.en: That can process things way faster than we can imagine.
cues.zh: 處理速度遠超想像。

cues.en: And that is what is facilitating deep learning.
cues.zh: 這支援了深度學習。

cues.en: So all of this brings us to the question: What is deep learning?
cues.zh: 帶出問題：什麼是深度學習？

cues.en: What is this whole neural network situation?
cues.zh: 神經網路是怎麼回事？

cues.en: What is going on? What are we even talking about here?
cues.zh: 到底在談什麼？

cues.en: And you've probably seen a picture of something like this.
cues.zh: 可能看過這種圖。

cues.en: So let's dive into it.
cues.zh: 深入看看。

cues.en: What is deep learning?
cues.zh: 什麼是深度學習？

cues.en: This gentleman over here, Jeffrey Hinton, is known as the godfather of deep learning.
cues.zh: 這位 Geoffrey Hinton，被稱深度學習教父。

cues.en: And he did research on deep learning in the 80s, and he's done lots and lots of work.
cues.zh: 八〇年代就研究，做了大量工作。

cues.en: Lots of research, papers that's he's published in deep learning.
cues.zh: 發表許多深度學習論文。

cues.en: Right now, he works at Google, so a lot of the things we're going to be talking about actually come from Jeffrey Hinton, and you can see a lot.
cues.zh: 當時在 Google，接下來很多內容來自 Hinton，你可以看到很多。

cues.en: He's got quite a lot of good YouTube videos, he explains things really well, so I highly recommend checking them out.
cues.zh: 有許多很棒的 YouTube 影片，解釋很好，強烈推薦。

cues.en: And so the idea behind deep learning is to look at the human brain.
cues.zh: 深度學習的想法，是觀察人腦。

cues.en: It's going to be quite a bit a lot of neuroscience coming up in these tutorials.
cues.zh: 接下來會有不少神經科學。

cues.en: And what we're trying to do here is to mimic how the human brain operates.
cues.zh: 試著模仿人腦如何運作。

cues.en: We don't know that much. We don't know everything about the human brain.
cues.zh: 我們了解不多，並非全知。

cues.en: But that little amount that we know we want to mimic it and recreate it.
cues.zh: 但想模仿、重建所知的一小部分。

cues.en: And why is it that?
cues.zh: 為什麼？

cues.en: Well, because the human brain seems to be the one of the most powerful tools on this planet for learning.
cues.zh: 因為人腦似乎是地球上最強的學習工具之一。

cues.en: For learning, adapting skills, and applying them.
cues.zh: 學習、適應技能、應用。

cues.en: And if computers could copy that, then we can just leverage what natural selection has.
cues.zh: 電腦若能複製，就能運用天擇

cues.en: Or it can decide it for us.
cues.zh: 為我們決定的成果。

cues.en: All those kind of algorithms that it has decided are the best, we can just leverage that.
cues.zh: 運用它決定最好的那些演算法。

cues.en: Like re-inventing the bicycle right?
cues.zh: 不用重新發明輪子，對吧？

cues.en: So let's see how this works.
cues.zh: 看看如何。

cues.en: Here we've got some neurons, so these are neurons which are having smeared onto glass and being looked at under a microscope with some coloring.
cues.zh: 一些神經元，塗在玻璃上、染色，在顯微鏡下看。

cues.en: And this is, you can see what they look like.
cues.zh: 可以看到外觀。

cues.en: So they have a like a body, they have these branches.
cues.zh: 有細胞體、分支。

cues.en: And they have like tails and so on.
cues.zh: 還有尾巴等等。

cues.en: You can see they have like a nucleus inside in the middle.
cues.zh: 中間有細胞核。

cues.en: And that's basically what a neuron looks like.
cues.zh: 神經元基本如此。

cues.en: In the human brain, there's approximately a hundred billion neurons altogether.
cues.zh: 人腦約一千億個。

cues.en: So these are individual neurons, there are actually modern neurons.
cues.zh: 這些是個別神經元，其實是運動神經元。

cues.en: Because they're bigger, they're easier to see.
cues.zh: 比較大，易觀察。

cues.en: But, nevertheless, there's a hundred billion neurons in the human brain.
cues.zh: 總之人腦一千億個。

cues.en: And each neuron is connected to as many as a thousand of its neighbors.
cues.zh: 每個最多連接約一千個鄰近神經元。

cues.en: So to give you a picture of this, this is what it looks like.
cues.zh: 給你看畫面。

cues.en: This is an actual dia, section of the human brain.
cues.zh: 這是真實人腦切片。

cues.en: And this is the cerebellum, which is this part of your brain.
cues.zh: 小腦，在這裡。

cues.en: At the back, it's responsible for like motorics and for, you know, keeping your balance, and some language capabilities and stuff like that.
cues.zh: 後方，負責動作、平衡，以及某些語言能力等等。

cues.en: So this is just to show how vast how many neurons there are.
cues.zh: 只是展示數量多龐大。

cues.en: Like billions and billions and billions of neurons all connecting your brain.
cues.zh: 數十億、數十億神經元在腦中互連。

cues.en: It's not like talking about five hundred or a thousand, or million. This is billions of neurons in there.
cues.zh: 不是五百、一千或一百萬，是數十億。

cues.en: And yeah, so, that's what we're going to try to recreate.
cues.zh: 這就是想重建的。

cues.en: So how do we recreate this in a computer?
cues.zh: 電腦怎麼重建？

cues.en: Well, we recreate an artificial structure called an artificial neural net.
cues.zh: 建人工結構，叫人工神經網路。

cues.en: Where we have nodes or neurons.
cues.zh: 有節點或神經元。

cues.en: And we're gonna have some neurons for input value, so these are values that you know about a certain situation.
cues.zh: 有輸入值神經元，代表已知情境資訊。

cues.en: So, for instance, you're modeling something.
cues.zh: 例如建模。

cues.en: You want to predict something, you're always going to want to have some input something to start your predictions off.
cues.zh: 想預測，總需要一些輸入作為起點。

cues.en: And then, that's called the input layer.
cues.zh: 叫輸入層。

cues.en: Then you have the output, so that's value that you want to predict. Whether that's a surprise, or there's, is somebody going to leave the bank or stay in the bank?
cues.zh: 再輸出，要預測的值；例如股價，或顧客離開、留在銀行？

cues.en: Is this a fraudulent transaction or is this a real transaction?
cues.zh: 詐欺還是真實交易？

cues.en: And so on.
cues.zh: 等等。

cues.en: So that's going to be output layer.
cues.zh: 這是輸出層。

cues.en: And in between, we're going to have a hidden layer.
cues.zh: 中間有隱藏層。

cues.en: So, as you can see, in your brain, you have so many neurons, so some information is coming in through your eyes, ears, nose.
cues.zh: 腦有很多神經元，資訊從眼、耳、鼻進來。

cues.en: So you're basically your senses.
cues.zh: 就是感官。

cues.en: And then it's not just going to right away to the output where you have the result.
cues.zh: 不會立刻到輸出結果。

cues.en: It's going through all of these billions and billions and billions of neurons before it gets to the output.
cues.zh: 先經數十億神經元，再到輸出。

cues.en: And this is the whole concept behind it that we're going to model the brain, so we need these hidden layers that are there before the output.
cues.zh: 整體概念是模擬大腦，所以輸出前需要隱藏層。

cues.en: So the input layer, neurons are connected to the hidden layer.
cues.zh: 輸入層神經元連隱藏層。

cues.en: Neurons in the hidden layer, neurons are connected to the output value.
cues.zh: 隱藏層神經元連輸出值。

cues.en: And so, this is pretty cool, but what is this all about?
cues.zh: 很酷，但到底意義何在？

cues.en: Where is the deep learning here?
cues.zh: 深度學習在哪？

cues.en: Why is it called deep learning?
cues.zh: 為什麼叫深度？

cues.en: There's nothing deep in here.
cues.zh: 這裡沒什麼深的。

cues.en: Well, this is kind of like an option, which one might call "shallow learning".
cues.zh: 這種可能叫淺層學習。

cues.en: Where there isn't much deep going on.
cues.zh: 沒太多深度。

cues.en: But why is it called deep learning? Well, because then we take this to the next level.
cues.zh: 為何深度？因為再往下一層次。

cues.en: We separate it even further, and we have not just one hidden layer, we have lots and lots and lots of hidden layers.
cues.zh: 進一步，不只一個隱藏層，而很多很多。

cues.en: And then we connect everything just like in the human brain.
cues.zh: 像人腦連接一切。

cues.en: Connect everything, inter connect everything, and that's how the input values of process through all these hidden layers, just like in the human brain,
cues.zh: 全部互連，輸入經所有隱藏層處理，像人腦，

cues.en: and then we have an output value.
cues.zh: 再有輸出。

cues.en: And now we're talking deep learning.
cues.zh: 現在才是深度學習。

cues.en: So that's what deep learning is all about on a very abstract level.
cues.zh: 這是非常抽象層次的概念。

cues.en: In the further tutorials, we're going to dissect and dive deep into deep learning.
cues.zh: 之後仔細拆解、深入。

cues.en: And by the end of it, you will know what deep learning is all about, and you'll know how to apply it in your projects.
cues.zh: 最後知道它是什麼、怎麼用在專案。

cues.en: I'm super excited about this, can't wait to get started.
cues.zh: 很期待，迫不及待。

cues.en: And I look forward to seeing you on the next tutorial.
